action: Osaka residents and businesses: do not open links or attachments in unexpected emails claiming to be from the city, never enter IDs, passwords, PINs or card details, and check notices on the official city website instead.
exec: A supplier's supplier was the weak point: the city's own systems were not entered, yet over a million residents' addresses are now phishing targets.
plain: Osaka's city government says someone broke into an outside email-sending service it relies on. More than a million email addresses of people who use the city's online services were exposed, plus about 48,000 from a shopping voucher scheme.

key_findings: Unauthorised access hit an outside email delivery service used by the city's Administrative Online System; system provider TKC reported the findings.
1,078,713 email addresses are affected, a count driven by a notice sent to all registered users on September 16, 2026.
Affected are people who received system emails between July 1 and October 31, 2026, such as registration, login and application notices.
A second final report covers the Premium Voucher 2026 scheme: 33,868 user and 14,669 store email addresses, with no access to the voucher management system confirmed.
Neither report names the email delivery service or explains how the intruder got in; individual notification is still under consideration.
recommendations: Do not open links or attachments in unexpected emails, even if they claim to come from the city or its online system.
Do not enter IDs, passwords, PINs or credit card details, and do not pay any fee demanded by email.
Verify suspicious messages through the official Osaka City website, not through links in the email.
The city will require detailed reports from its contractors and review how personal data is handled in outside services.

summary: The City of Osaka's final reports of November 13 say a third party got into an outside email delivery service used by two city programmes. For the Administrative Online System, supplied by TKC, 1,078,713 email addresses sent mail between July 1 and October 31 are affected. For the Premium Voucher 2026 scheme, 33,868 user and 14,669 store addresses are affected. Only email addresses are described as exposed.
title: City of Osaka: breach of outside email delivery service exposed over 1 million email addresses

validation.note: Reviewed against the original City of Osaka document: two final reports issued on November 13. Neither names the email delivery service.
